So `SessionStart` is conceptually “session-level”, but operationally it is deferred until the first turn starts. That matches what you’re seeing: the banner only appears after the first prompt is submitted, because that is the first time Codex enters the hook runtime.

There is no earlier public hook in the current Codex hook set:
- `SessionStart`
- `UserPromptSubmit`
- `Stop`
- `PreToolUse`

- No, I don’t see another hook that fires earlier than the current `SessionStart`.
- In Codex, “before first prompt is submitted” does not seem to be hookable via the current hook system.
- What you have is likely the best available behavior unless Codex adds a true startup/UI-ready hook.

can you tell me which permissions the OPENAI_API_KEY needs?

`OPENAI_API_KEY` does not need admin/org-management permissions for this workflow. It just needs to be a normal API key that can make model requests.

Practical answer:
- `Read Only`: not enough
- `Restricted`: should work if it allows write access to the inference endpoints Codex uses
- `All`: simplest/safest if you just want CI to work

What I could verify:
- OpenAI keys support `All`, `Restricted`, and `Read Only` permissions, and `Restricted` can set `None` / `Read` / `Write` per endpoint: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8867743-assign-api-key-permissions
- Project keys are managed at the project level; no special admin key is needed just to use an API key in a project: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9186755-managing-projects-in-the-api-platform
- RBAC is separate from runtime API-key use: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rbac

My recommendation for this repo:
- use a project-scoped secret key
- start with `All` if you want the least friction in CI
- if you want to lock it down, switch to `Restricted` and allow write access to the model/inference endpoints Codex CLI uses

- I did not find an official source that explicitly lists the exact endpoint set Codex CLI calls under the hood, so “Restricted with minimal endpoint set” would need one quick real-world test after you create the key.

content.text: I have the failure mode. I’m checking the Codex bootstrap path once more to confirm whether CI is relying only on `OPENAI_API_KEY` and never creating a real Codex auth config, because that’s what the job log points to.

Yes. The CI wiring itself worked, but Codex never got a usable authenticated request path during the test step.

What happened in that job:
- `Install agent CLI`: succeeded
- `Bootstrap agent`: succeeded
- `Run E2E Tests`: failed for almost every test

The key lines in the failing step are:

- WebSocket transport hit repeated `500 Internal Server Error` on `wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses`
- Codex then fell back to HTTPS
- HTTPS requests failed with `401 Unauthorized: Missing bearer or basic authentication in header`

So the immediate failure was: Codex made unauthenticated HTTPS requests in CI.

Why this likely happened:
